title: Steno: three directions
subtitle: Gray skeletons for the AI meeting-notes app. The only color is the swatch strip. Same copy in all three.

directions.why: A yellow legal pad with a red margin line. The hero is the product: a notes page writing itself during a call.
directions.from: the outlier (warm, product-as-hero) beats the dark AI default.
directions.paletteNames: legal pad · ink navy · margin red · rule blue
directions.logo: 'Steno' in navy with the red margin line as the stem of the t.
directions.favicon: a yellow page with a red margin line.
directions.wildcard: the red margin line runs down the whole page, with call timestamps (00:14, 03:52...) written in it next to each section.

directions.why: Bright white page; the hero is a video call with captions burning in word by word. The title itself is a caption.
directions.from: every AI notes page is dark with glow; captions are black bars on light, the opposite.
desktop: [You]  We'll take the notes. You run the meeting.
CAPTION TYPES IN WORD BY WORD, SPEAKER LABEL
order: Who said what, who owes what
directions.paletteNames: screen white · caption black · highlight yellow · call gray
directions.fonts: Atkinson Hyperlegible 700 (titles and captions, chosen for legibility like real subtitles) · IBM Plex Mono
directions.logo: 'Steno' white on a black caption bar.
directions.favicon: a black caption bar with a yellow underline.
directions.wildcard: the spoken word highlights in yellow as it's 'heard', the same way the product follows the call.

directions.why: A stenotype paper tape runs down the page; the coded strokes on it turn into clean notes beside it as you scroll.
directions.from: court stenography is where 'every word, nothing lost' already exists.
directions.paletteNames: tape cream · ink · recording lamp · tape edge
directions.fonts: IBM Plex Sans Condensed 700 (titles) · IBM Plex Mono (the steno strokes)
directions.logo: 'STENO' in condensed caps, with a green recording dot.
directions.favicon: a strip of tape with a green dot.
directions.wildcard: the tape keeps feeding down through every section; scrolling is the tape moving.
